title: Traffic-aware SLO taxonomy and circuit-breaker playbook for model variants
creator: Leah Thompson
description:
Goal: Establish a unified SLO/SLI taxonomy and operational policy that is traffic-aware (distinguishes user-facing vs internal traffic), supports per-model and per-endpoint weighting, and ties directly to automated circuit-breaker behavior and regional load-shedding. This ticket covers definition, metrics, thresholds, and the operator runbook for safe automatic interventions (failover, degrade, shed) when error budgets burn or regional capacity drops. The output will be a short operator playbook, a set of new SLI tags and aggregation rules in our metrics pipeline, and a set of pre-configured circuit-breaker profiles suitable for low-latency chat endpoints, batch/embedding endpoints, and admin/internal routes.

Why now: Recent incidents highlighted that uniform SLO rules cause poor signal (mixing bulk embeddings with chat), and that our current circuit-breaker thresholds are disconnected from error-budget burn rates and regional capacity indicators. We need a single, auditable taxonomy that feeds the Console and the autoscaler/circuit-breaker controllers so we can both alert and automatically protect downstream systems with predictable behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A1: SLO taxonomy documented and approved by SRE/Platform/Product with examples for chat, embeddings, and reranking
A2: New SLI tags and aggregation rules implemented in observability pipeline (prometheus/tempo/metrics-backend) and unit-tested
A3: At least three circuit-breaker profile templates (chat-low-latency, embeddings-high-throughput, internal-admin) implemented and configurable by model/route in Console
A4: Runbook with step-by-step actions for error-budget exhaustion, regional capacity loss, and progressive rollback is published and linked in incident templates
A5: Demo failover test executed in staging simulating 30% regional capacity loss, and behavior logged and reviewed
decisions: D1: Use weighted SLI aggregation (weight = request_cost * tier_multiplier) to compute per-model error budgets rather than simple counts
D2: Tie circuit-breaker tripping to a combined signal: 10m request error-rate AND 5m rolling error-budget burn-rate > 3x baseline
D3: For multi-region failover, prefer gradual shifting (10% steps every 30s) with canary requests until healthy thresholds met
D4: Default load-shedding order: non-critical background tasks -> low-tier embeddings -> chat responses downgraded to cached or partial responses
D5: Include a manual override toggle in Console that annotates incidents and inhibits automated failover for legal/compliance customers
runbook_summary: Operators should follow a three-stage remediation flow: 1) Assess signal (SLI error-rate, burn-rate, region capacity metrics). 2) Activate profile (apply circuit-breaker template and start progressive region shift). 3) If error-budget still burning after 10 minutes, escalate to full shedding policy and open incident with postmortem template. Each stage includes safe rollback steps and an annotated checklist for communication (status page, affected customers).
rollout_plan: 1) Implement taxonomy and SLI tagging in staging metrics collector. 2) Ship circuit-breaker templates behind a feature flag. 3) Run chaos-style tests (regional capacity drop, traffic skew) in preprod to validate behaviors. 4) Enable in a limited set of low-risk endpoints for 48h. 5) Gradually expand to all endpoints and add to canary dashboards. 6) Post-release review and adjust thresholds based on burn-rate telemetry.
